history.summary: DUPLICATE FLAG: this row duplicates seq 1144 (id moteshwar-mahadev-temple-kashipur), which documents the same Moteshwar Mahadev (Bheem Shankar) Shiva temple at Chaiti/Ujjanak, Kashipur. The CSV row name 'Chaiti Devi Temple (Moteshwar Mahadev)' conflates two adjacent shrines on the same grounds: the Shakti shrine of Chaiti Devi (Maa Bal Sundari, covered by seq 1142, id chaiti-devi-temple-kashipur) and the Shiva shrine of Moteshwar Mahadev. A major Shiva shrine in the Ujjanak area of Kashipur, about 3 km from the bus station, on the banks of the Kosi. The temple's name comes from 'Mota' (large): the Shiva lingam is said to be too large to embrace with two hands and to keep growing. Local tradition calls this the Bheem Shankar Jyotirlingam, the Kama-roop (face) of Shiva, and counts it among the 12 Jyotirlingas - a disputed claim, since the widely recognised Bhimashankar Jyotirlinga is in Maharashtra; treat as a local claim. Sources conflict on age: temple websites claim 302 AD, while another says the structure is 12th century (verify). CSV town corrected from 'Udham Singh Nagar' to Kashipur.

name: Chaiti Devi Temple (Moteshwar Mahadev)
town_description: Kashipur is a historic city in the Terai region of Udham Singh Nagar district, with roots reaching back to the Vedic-age city of Ujjaini and the 7th-century Govishan visited by Chinese traveller Hiuen Tsang. Now a major industrial and educational city and the gateway to Kumaon, it hosts ancient temples, the Drona Sagar lake associated with Guru Dronacharya, and the famous annual Chaiti Mela.

travel.railway: Kashipur Junction Railway Station, about 3 km; linked to Delhi, Lucknow, Moradabad and Varanasi
travel.road: Near the Kashipur bus station (Arya Nagar/Ujjanak area); Kashipur is well connected by road to Delhi and other North Indian cities
